content.title: Sony is raising PS5 prices. Again.
content.text: (NEXSTAR/WDTN) – For the second time in just over seven months, Sony is raising the price for several PlayStation models by a not-insignificant amount. The price hikes will take effect for the PS5 (both base and digital editions), the PS5 Pro, and the PlayStation Portal Remote Player in April. The company announced the news in a blog post published Friday morning. Isabelle Tomatis, the vice president of global marketing for Sony Interactive Entertainment, said Sony’s decision to increase prices was driven by “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” “We know that price changes impact our community, and after careful evaluation, we found this was a necessary step to ensure we can continue delivering innovative, high-quality gaming experiences to players worldwide,” reads a portion of the blog post. The recommended retail price of a PS5 console is increasing $649.99, up from $549.99 (an 18% increase) and the PS5 Digital Edition will cost $599.99, up from $499.99 (a 20% increase). The PS5 Pro, meanwhile, jumps in price from $749.99 to $899.99 (another 20% increase) while the handheld PlayStation Portal gaming accessory is going from $199.99 to $249.99 (a 25% increase). ConsolePrice As Of April 2Current PricePercent ChangePlayStation 5 Digital Edition$599.99$499.9920%PlayStation 5$649.99$549.9918%PlayStation 5 Pro$899.99$749.9920%PlayStation Portal$249.99$199.9925% These recommended retail prices are effective as of April 2, Sony said. The PS5 and its Digital Edition were originally released in November 2020 at suggested retail prices of $499 and $399, respectively. The PS5 Pro, which launched in November 2024, originally cost $699.99. The PlayStation Portal was released in 2023 and priced at $199.99. Sony Interactive Entertainment had previously hiked prices for its PS5 models in August 2025, raising each by $50 over their original launch prices. At the time, Tomatis pointed to “a challenging economic environment.” A representative for PlayStation was not immediately available to share additional information on the factors that prompted the increases. But outlets including IGN and Bloomberg had speculated that a shortage of memory chips — due to an increase in demand for AI technologies — could be to blame. (IGN and The Verge had also pointed to President Trump’s tariffs as a factor for previous price hikes in the gaming industry). 📧 Have breaking news come to you: Subscribe to News 2 email alerts → Gamers who commented under PlayStation’s own blog post largely appeared to be disappointed or shocked by the PS5’s new pricing, with one calling it “insane” and another finding it “disgusting.” “I’ll never forget what it was like to buy a console three years after its release it already cost half the price, and the best part was that it was a slim version,” one person said. “If I did not already own a PS5 I would certainly would not buy one at that price,” another wrote.
